title: Regulatory Oversight and Licensing Authority
summary: The role of the Department of Livestock Services evolved from a general administrative reference in customs notifications to a central regulatory body responsible for licensing, monitoring, and approving imports of animal feed ingredients. The scope of its authority expanded to include verifying the end-use of imported goods and ensuring compliance with animal health standards.

evolution.scope: From passive entity mention to active regulatory gatekeeper.
evolution.procedure: Introduction of mandatory prior approval and annual demand assessment for imports.
evolution.enforcement: Shift from general oversight to specific monitoring of supply chains and end-use verification.

timeline.change: Formal nomenclature change from 'Poshu Shampad Odhidoptor' to 'Prani Shampad Odhidoptor' (Department of Livestock Services).
Established the Department as a mandatory licensing/registration authority for importers and introduced a monitoring mandate for the usage of imported goods in farms.
Expanded regulatory control to include mandatory prior approval for specific high-risk feed ingredients (MBM, Fish Meal) and formalized the reporting/clearance process.

Animal Feed and Veterinary Products: The importer must obtain an annual requirement assessment from the relevant department to receive clearance for importing raw materials for animal feed production. This clearance must be submitted to the relevant Commissioner of Customs.
Fish Feed Ingredients: Importers of specific protein concentrates and fish meal for fish feed must obtain prior approval from the Department of Fisheries. This requirement applies to products derived from fish or other non-animal sources, excluding meat and bone meal.
Commissioner of Customs: The importer is required to submit the official import clearance certificate issued by the relevant department to the Commissioner of Customs.
Department of Livestock Services: The Department of Livestock Services must provide prior approval for the import of specific animal feed ingredients such as meat and bone meal, fish meal, and protein concentrates. During the approval process, the importer must disclose the country of origin and the species of animal from which the product is derived.
Department of Fisheries: The Department of Fisheries is the authority responsible for granting prior approval for the import of fish feed ingredients, specifically protein concentrates and fish meal derived from sources other than animal-based materials.

Poultry and Dairy Farm: This entity is defined as an industrial establishment registered with either the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority or the Department of Livestock Services.

The entity is required to undergo a certification process to confirm that imported machinery, spare parts, and equipment are utilized for the balancing, modernization, replacement, and expansion of the farm.
Imported Machinery and Equipment: These goods are subject to verification regarding their utilization for the balancing, modernization, replacement, and expansion of registered poultry and dairy farms.
The importation details, including letter of credit, invoice, and bill of entry numbers, must be certified to validate the intended use of the equipment.
Breeders Association of Bangladesh: The association is empowered to issue formal certification regarding the usage of imported machinery and equipment by registered poultry and dairy farms.
